notice: The northern coast around AD 1 for Grind Strat (Sweden, Åland, Finland, Estonia): where the sea stood higher against today's land, 500 m cells, in steps of 8 years from AD 1 to 1219, where the 1219 coast takes over. An estimate: today's land uplift (NKG_RF17vel) bent to fit dated lake isolations (north Uppland), over GEBCO's heights; Kopli's neck is a hand-drawn cut. sgu.note: SGU's shore model is blocked (resource.sgu.se is not allowed): Sweden's AD 1 shore is the estimate, bent to north Uppland (Hedenström and Risberg), as the 1219 coast was bent to Stockholm.

kopli.about: Kopli (Tallinn): Kakumäe joined the mainland about 2800 cal BP, Kopli about 1000 years later (about AD 150) (Saarse and Vassiljev 2010). GEBCO's heights at 450 m cannot show the narrow low neck of the Kopli peninsula, so the island is a HAND-DRAWN CUT: the cells under the line below are sea until the year given and land after it. The line's place (across the low ground that joins the peninsula to the mainland, about 59.4465N from 24.655E to 24.725E, and carried on along the same line in both directions until it meets today's sea) is our own reading of today's map, not the paper's map: TO CHECK. It stands for an estimate, not a survey.
kopli.source: Saarse, L. and Vassiljev, J. (2010), Holocene shore displacement in the surroundings of Tallinn, North Estonia, Estonian Journal of Earth Sciences 59(3), 207-215, doi:10.3176/earth.2010.3.03

meta.older: Not used: Lohja 6.23 m at 2240 cal BP (its place in the Rosentau database is not yet read, TO CHECK) and Prassi on Hiiumaa (a limiting point). SGU's shore model (resource.sgu.se) is blocked: Sweden's AD 1 shore is the estimate, as in 1219.
